author: Asawin Suebsaeng

When you talk to people close to President Donald Trump, they will be quick to
tell you that he's mad at the TV again, and he's mad about Republicans who
don't want to talk about him. And that's why he's now forcing the federal
government to run [another](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-
features/trump-kristi-noem-200-million-dhs-ad-campaign-thanks-
president-1235276324/) pro-Trump propaganda campaign that Americans are paying
for with their tax dollars.

The first such TV ad features the deeply unpopular president railing against
"communists," over a song pleading "LOVE ME," with a
[disclaimer](https://x.com/DeFede/status/2102928979254792260) that it's being
"paid for by the U.S. government."
[Watchdogs](https://www.citizen.org/article/white-house-spending-taxpayer-
dollars-for-propaganda-purposes/) and
[lawmakers](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/09/24/ad-boosting-
trump-paid-by-taxpayers-airing-la-chicago/) say the ad violates federal laws
that bar the use of federal money for propaganda purposes, and prohibit
federal employees from using official resources for politics. Some elected
Democrats are [demanding
answers](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/09/24/us/Maggie-Hassan-
Letter-Susie-Wiles.html) from the White House. Trump's running these ads with
taxpayer dollars despite
[his](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/18/us/politics/trump-pac-spending-
violation.html) political operation having an obscene amount of cash to burn.

Several longtime GOP operatives working on competitive 2026 races told
**Zeteo** that they thought the "Love Me" ad campaign was a bad idea, with one
consultant close to the Trump White House saying: "It was kind of pathetic."
Others in and close to the Trump administration weren't thrilled about it,
either.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

The White House wasn't done, though. Trump's administration is also planning
to [run an ad](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-focused-ad-campaign-
taxpayers/) touting the president's successful plot to kidnap Venezuelan
leader Nicolas Maduro, and it's running [a 60-second
ad](https://x.com/AdImpact_Pol/status/2103459952484323537) featuring Trump
speaking at Mount Rushmore about how he's brought about "the golden age of
America." The White House [calls](https://zeteo.com/p/netanyahu-slams-mamdani-
and-piker) these taxpayer-funded propaganda ads "public service
announcements," and
[insists](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/09/presidential-public-
service-announcements-are-nothing-new/) they are "very clearly not campaign
ads."

So, why does this TV ad campaign exist? Beyond the fact that the Trump-Vance
administration is plowing an ungodly amount of public money and resources into
myriad initiatives designed specifically to [make President Trump feel good
about himself](https://zeteo.com/p/donald-trump-pyongyang), there is one
major, 2026-related reason that you're seeing the "LOVE ME" ad on your
television.
